question: How does Caddy replace a running configuration without discarding the old one before the new applications are ready, and where can the handoff fail?

observations.text: The API handler marshals the new config to JSON only after applying the mutation, and if unchanged it returns early without reload.
After marshalling, the handler indexes config objects. If indexing fails, it restores rawCfg from rawCfgJSON and returns an error.
The handoff function unsyncedDecodeAndRun is called with the new config JSON; on success it swaps the current context and then stops the old apps.
In unsyncedDecodeAndRun, the new config is unmarshaled and then run via run(newCfg, true) which provisions and starts all apps.
If run fails, unsyncedDecodeAndRun returns an error, and the caller restores the old config from rawCfgJSON.
The run function starts apps one by one; if any app fails to start, it stops all already started apps and returns an error.
Old config remains running until the new config's apps are fully started and the context is swapped, ensuring no downtime from discarded old config.
After successful start, the run function calls finishSettingUp which may fail; if so, run returns an error and old config is restored.
In provisionContext, the admin server is replaced before provisioning apps; failure here causes run to return error.
The unsyncedStop function stops each app and cancels the old context, but is only called after the new context is swapped.
If unsyncedDecodeAndRun fails, the API handler restores rawCfg to the old config and returns an error, preserving the running old config.
